text: The NSRC’s work and the changes it proposed can be grouped into three broad thrusts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: First, how to maximise the contributions of National Servicemen; second, improving the NS experience; and third, enhancing support and recognition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As all Members of the House know, our birth rates are low and what this then translates into would be smaller NS cohorts 18 years hence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In this context, the SAF has to find different ways to continue to optimise the deployment of every resource and every National Serviceman, in order for our defence to remain robust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman and Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked for updates on the medical classification system review and functional assessments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Minister Ng Eng Hen had given the overall view yesterday and I will elaborate on that.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Functional assessment allows us to assess the NSFs’ abilities to perform physical tasks required for the job in order to better match them to vocations with greater precision and to enable them to discharge their duties well and safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These assessments have been developed in consultation with external physiotherapy specialists, alongside SAF physiotherapists from our Centre of Excellence for Soldier Performance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They have also been trialled prior to implementation to ensure that the outcomes would be effective discharge of duties, effectiveness in the outcomes that the SAF seeks from the protection angle and, at the same time, safety of our Servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These tests will be administered by trained SAF physiotherapists when the pre-enlistees report for medical screening, according to established protocols.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These pre-enlistees will then be deployed to the relevant vocations according to their abilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: At the same time, to further expand deployment opportunities, the SAF has continued to redesign existing jobs for our NSFs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For instance, take the example of the redesign of the medic role.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Leveraging advances in medical technology and efforts to define the physical demands required for each specific role, Servicemen of varying physical capabilities can now be deployed as medics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This approach has enabled the SAF to maximise our Servicemen’s potential to contribute to the SAF’s operational requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, I have been speaking of optimising deployments from the angle of physical fitness and job requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: But there is also another important angle which is equally important and this concerns the skills, knowledge and expertise of our Servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our population may be small, but it is increasingly well-educated and well-skilled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Future conflicts will not be solely decided by force numbers and sizes, though these are obviously relevant, but it would also be influenced – to an increasing extent – by technology and know-how.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF should increasingly grow and tap on the expertise of our National Servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked about MINDEF’s plans for Work-Learn schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We have established Work-Learn schemes for several critical skills-based SAF vocations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Eligible NSFs can join these schemes to receive accredited training and education from Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), whilst performing their NS roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Servicemen benefit from these qualifications and the work experience gained.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF is also able to tap on these Servicemen’s expertise for a sustained period of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The first Work-Learn scheme was introduced in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In the years ahead, we expect to expand the Work-Learn schemes to cover more roles and vocations, based on the SAF’s operational requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This year, the SAF will introduce another two Work-Learn schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: One is the Digital Work-Learn scheme for eligible Servicemen to pursue undergraduate degrees in areas, such as Computer Engineering and Data Science.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The other is the Work-Study Diploma for Supply Supervisors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our efforts to optimise expertise-based deployment also cover Operationally-Ready NS, or ORNS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: A good number of our NSmen acquire expertise through their civilian careers and these are relevant to the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: A key priority for the SAF is to identify these NSmen during ORNS and redeploy them where their expertise can be put to best use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Last year, I spoke about the establishment of the Expertise Deployment Centre within the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: With dedicated resources devoted to identifying and redeploying NSmen with relevant expertise, the number of expertise-based redeployments has gone up considerably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: One of our redeployed NSmen is ME4A Jeremy Yeap.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Jeremy Yeap is a lawyer specialising in dispute resolution and he wanted to contribute further with the skills and experience that he has in his role as a lawyer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: ME4A Jeremy, who had served as an Air Force Engineer, was redeployed in 2021 and now provides specialist legal advice to commanders as part of SAF operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked how expertise-based redeployment would be expanded.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: While we invest significant efforts to optimise deployment, we must not forget that a strong SAF is contingent upon the commitment and morale of its fighting force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This brings me to the second thrust of NSRC’s work, which is that of improving the NS experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: A number of Members have asked about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: At the core of that experience are the NSmen and we have, therefore, designed our processes around that so that the NSman can be very well-focused for his training, knowing that the organisation is there behind him, cares about him, does everything to make sure that his contributions are maximised for the protection of this country, and takes care of his safety and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Yesterday, Minister Ng Eng Hen touched on our plans to automate the Make-Up Pay claims system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: At present, the filing of such claims is done manually by NSmen and their employers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Later this year, MINDEF will introduce an automated system which draws on income-related information from CPF Board and IRAS to compute the Make-Up Pay amounts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NSmen and their employers will be provided the opportunity to review the computed amounts to see if they agree.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: If no objections are raised, the amount will then be paid out to them automatically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For the bulk of NSmen and their employers, this greatly simplifies the process and saves time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Those who believe that the computed amounts are not up-to-date can certainly submit additional information for recalculation, so that the right amounts are paid out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Today, some NSmen, mostly from lower-income segments, may receive income from informal job roles, gig economy employment or other payments, such as allowances and incentives, which may not be captured in CPF Board's or IRAS' databases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As mentioned by Minister Ng Eng Hen, along with automating Make-Up Pay computation, we will be implementing a base NS pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For In-Camp Training of shorter durations, the allowance will be pro-rated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Aside from automating Make-Up Pay claims and base NS pay, allow me now to also talk about two other initiatives which will improve our servicemen’s NS experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This will replace the existing NS Portal and will provide a more seamless experience for our servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our National Servicemen perform several transactions with MINDEF/SAF throughout their NS journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The idea is to centralise these transactions and essential NS services onto the OneNS platform and render it more accessible via a single mobile application or a revamped web portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For a start, NSmen can look forward to enhanced Call-Up and Deferment eServices, to facilitate preparation for ICT.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Other eServices will be rolled out subsequently and progressively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MINDEF has also collaborated with the Smart Nation Digital Government Group to digitally deliver NS recognition benefits to our National Servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Since November last year, MINDEF has been disbursing the NS Excellence Awards and Celebratory Gifts in the form of e-credits that can be accessed via LifeSG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In the past, recipients received their benefits in the form of physical vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: With this change, they are now able to receive and redeem these credits conveniently via the use of their mobile devices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The credits can be used at both online and brick-and-mortar shops that accept payment by PayNow QR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Thus far, through surveys, we found that 97% of surveyed users had reported satisfaction with this improvement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Come April this year, servicemen will also be able to use their credits with merchants that accept NETS QR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: With this change, an even broader range of merchants will be able to benefit, including those who operate in heartland shops and hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Obviously, with this greater array of merchants and merchandise, it will also be a value-add to our NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MINDEF will move our other cash and voucher-based recognition schemes, such as the cash payments for NS HOME, onto LifeSG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Quite apart from the convenience that this will bring to our NSmen, this will also greatly contribute to our national drive to foster e-payments adoption and to go green and paperless.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our National Servicemen who have received NS recognition benefits via the LifeSG mobile application will receive SMS notifications that these credits have gone into their account.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are very conscious that, in sending out these SMS notifications, these should not be mistaken as scams, and we will ensure that our SMSes will have no clickable links.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This brings me to the third thrust of the NSRC’s work, which is that of enhancing recognition and support for our National Servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our National Servicemen contribute to defence during their two years of National Service and at every subsequent In-Camp Training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: There is sacrifice, from both them, as well as, we hear from Members, through the support of their families as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked about our recognition initiatives for our National Servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The additional $2,000 cash will be paid out as credits into our National Servicemen’s LifeSG mobile application.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This complements the current NS HOME payment, of which the bulk is disbursed into the National Servicemen’s CPF accounts for long-term financial needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As I have explained earlier, these credits can be used at merchants ranging from those that operate on e-commerce platforms to brick-and-mortar shops as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond recognition, we also want to provide our servicemen and their families with peace of mind when they participate in NS activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We have reviewed this and, come 2023, we will increase the coverage to $300,000 each.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This will help ensure that the financial support and protection we accord our National Servicemen remain relevant and adequate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, the NSRC has completed its reviews, which have been significant in strengthening the NS system and the SAF’s operational effectiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And we want to thank the co-chairs and members of the Committee for the good work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Aside from the changes the Minister for Defence and I have outlined, the NSRC has made three other broad recommendations, which we will continue to follow up on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will continue to work on, first, enhancing our training and leadership development programmes for National Servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Second, better equipping our NSFs with transferable skills and preparing them for their transition to studies or work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And, third, better supporting pre-enlistees as they balance their NS-related obligations with personal pursuits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I shall now move on to speak about another topic which is critical – training safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As we continue to enhance the NS system, our safety practices on the ground must also continue to be robust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF, therefore, places a very strong emphasis on strengthening our safety culture through regular audits and inspections, by leveraging technology and constantly reminding both commanders and men of the importance to internalise the safety culture itself – look after yourself, look after one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked about the third External Review Panel on SAF Safety, or ERPSS, which MINDEF/SAF started last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Panel was established to review the SAF’s safety management systems and to make recommendations to improve safety in the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: A positive observation made by the Panel was the continual enhancements to the Safety Management System at our Basic Military Training Centre, or BMTC, where a slew of safety and mental health support measures has been implemented to better help recruits transit from civilian life into military life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Panel also noted the efforts to scaffold safety training across the leadership schools to ensure that our commanders understand and will conduct training safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The ERPSS will continue to highlight best practices from industry during their continued visits to our ground units.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Aside from the ERPSS, we have, internally, the SAF Inspector-General’s Office.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF Inspector-General’s Office has commenced its second two-year audit cycle of all SAF formations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Compared to the first audit cycle, commanders and servicemen were observed to have taken even more ownership in upholding safety practices and displayed more awareness towards potential safety hazards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Going forward, the SAF will continue to sustain our emphasis on safety policies and processes and to ensure that safety lessons will be passed on, even as we see the turnover of servicemen, because it is in the nature of our NS system that you have cohorts who come in and train and they may leave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: But we must ensure that the safety culture is entrenched and it is practised and improved upon, and we will do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This would provide better awareness of safety situations and make safety promotion more targeted and, therefore, reduce the risk and likelihood of incidents recurring elsewhere within the SAF that are similar to the original occurrence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: However, as I have said, safety is not just the responsibility of commanders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SafeGuardian mobile application, which I spoke about at Committee of Supply (COS) 2020, has played a significant role in enabling our servicemen to report safety hazards and near misses in a timely manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SafeGuardian mobile application has empowered our servicemen to take greater ownership of their own safety and the safety of those around them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about other recent efforts to enhance training safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We recognise that rising ambient temperatures due to climate change will increasingly impact the well-being of our servicemen and the effectiveness of our training and operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Therefore, we look ahead to see what is it that we need to do in order to sustain our ability to train safely but effectively and upkeep our operational readiness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This centre will conduct forward-looking research on heat mitigation strategies and develop more fundamental approaches to prevent heat injury in the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, as we celebrate 55 years of NS this year, we all recognise that NS remains the cornerstone of our national defence and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We must continue to build on the previous generations’ efforts and dedication to the protection of this country and the strengthening of our NS system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is a work that will never cease, and the NSRC's recommendations will add to this effort and will put us in good stead as we continue on this journey to ensure that Singapore will forever be secure and free.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister for Defence Dr Ng spoke about the global geopolitical shifts, transnational threats and the attendant impact on Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Increasingly, the security challenges that test us will lie outside of traditional battlefields – some call this "grey zone" contestation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Now, more than ever, our investments in both the SAF and Total Defence continue to be crucial as Singapore’s bulwark against crises, challenges and potential aggression.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In 1984, we launched Total Defence in the context of a conventional threat landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Both then and now, our Total Defence pillars reinforce our belief that a strong foundation for our defence goes beyond the military domain and requires a whole-of-society response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over the years, we have faced numerous challenges, from pandemics to economic recessions, to terrorism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the last two years, we have grappled with the COVID-19 pandemic as it upended our lives and stress-tested us as a nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It has pressured our healthcare systems and strained our supply chains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many amongst us have lost jobs and had to pivot to new sectors or roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And just when it felt like we had turned a corner with the vaccines, there have been new variants like Delta and Omicron.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While this has not been a conventional war, it has been a crisis that has impacted all of us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are dealing with an unknown threat – COVID-19 – which, even today, remains elusive and ever-evolving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In order to meet this threat and protect one another from the virus, we have needed a whole-of-society response through Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We understand that Member of Parliament Cheng Li Hui is interested in this topic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Let us take our vaccination programme as an example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am heartened that many have stepped up in support of our national vaccine effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One example is National Serviceman Captain Dr Shane Abucewicz-Tan, a medical officer for the Home Vaccination Team, who supported COVID-19 operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He conducted household visits as part of the Home Vaccination Programme, ensuring that Singaporeans who were immobile and immunocompromised could receive their vaccinations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Another example is the Singapore Federation of Chinese Clan Associations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It put together videos in dialects, such as Hakka, Cantonese and Teochew, to encourage seniors to receive their vaccinations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Indeed, we have looked out for and supported one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In 2020, the migrant worker community was disproportionately impacted when COVID-19 began spreading in the dormitories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am grateful to our partners who have made this possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Academic institutions, such as the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore, also helped make the site more sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For instance, they tested lightweight solar panels and piloted energy storage solutions, which could be scaled to other temporary sites like these and contribute to our sustainability efforts in the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There are many contributions beyond these and too many heroes to name today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The threats to our way of life – our sense of stability and security – come in many forms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: A study by Check Point Research found that Singapore saw a 145% increase in cyberattacks from 2020 to 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The healthcare sector was the most targeted sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Throughout the pandemic, fear-mongers have spread falsehoods about variants and the ill-effects of vaccines, which have directly threatened public health and, if not, weakened trust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As Singapore imports 90% of our food, we are highly dependent on continued access to quality food supplies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Threats to our supply chains, natural disasters and climate change have affected our supplies and food prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Minister Ng touched on the situation in Ukraine in his speech yesterday.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As we watch events unfold, it is a lesson in real-time for Singaporeans on how a country’s stability can be threatened on multiple fronts, including cyberattacks, information campaigns and border threats, and all these ahead of military aggression.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is tragic and sad how events in Ukraine have unfolded.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: What is now clear to me, and I hope for many Singaporeans, too, is that we must always be ready and we can only depend on ourselves for our defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Total Defence – being able to defend ourselves economically, socially and even psychologically – has to be every Singaporean’s responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As threats become more complex, multidimensional and multifaceted, how can we ensure that we are ever ready to meet them?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Member of Parliament Denise Phua asked about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: How can Total Defence continue to galvanise every Singaporean for our survival, security and success?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is with these questions in mind that we embarked on a review of Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the past 16 months, we heard from over 2,000 Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We asked them how Total Defence might better rally Singaporeans in times of crisis and this was even before the Ukraine situation happened.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: From these conversations, we learnt that Total Defence has room to be more resonant and relatable, even as the actions within the six pillars remain relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some found it too abstract, prescriptive and focused on present-day threats at the expense of emerging challenges, while some others did not want to be told what Total Defence was about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Instead, they wanted to be proactive, and wanted space to contribute ideas and efforts towards shaping a Singapore that they aspired to see.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am grateful for the feedback, which will guide our ongoing review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have started building on some of these suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I say "more", because many Singaporeans have already stepped up to support the causes that they care about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, more people are choosing to buy local produce and dabble in community gardening to strengthen food security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: A sandbox is a safe environment where you can test ideas and programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And that is what we hope this can be: a space that links ideas to resources, to turn ideas into prototypes and prototypes into solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We look forward to supporting projects that target today’s most salient challenges, such as cyber threats, food insecurity, are some examples.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some ideas we have heard so far include workshops to increase awareness of cybersecurity and campaigns to promote environmentally sustainable habits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The possibilities are vast and we look forward to Members' contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also continue conversations with Singaporeans to expand and reimagine the actions that we can take for Total Defence – both in the current security environment and for the challenges that we will face in the near future or the future to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As the security environment continues to evolve, Singaporeans must be aware of the threats to our sovereignty and stability as well as vulnerabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Only then can we understand the roles that we might play and how some of these will impact on our actions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Singapore Discovery Centre (SDC), for one, will be transformed to better tell Singapore’s stories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Member of Parliament Chong Kee Hiong asked about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SDC has made strides in Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) and environmental sustainability, and in recent months, refreshed its galleries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the upper gallery, an AR, first-person shooter game, takes visitors back to the Battle of Bukit Chandu on 14 February 1942.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: That day, even though Lieutenant Adnan Saidi and the Malay Regiment soldiers were outnumbered and eventually ran out of supplies, they fought valiantly against the Japanese Army and refused to surrender.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As players hunker down behind sandbags, they will experience how the regiment defended themselves against waves of opponents and they will also understand the grit and determination that Lieutenant Adnan and his men had shown despite the odds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In that interactive space, a simulated digital environment allows visitors to experience Singapore’s history and the threats that we faced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Startups and students, including those in the AR/VR domain, can also use a new incubator space to collaborate on projects, experiment with technology and bring ideas to life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SDC has also been investing in innovative energy solutions and renewables, and implementing various energy efficiency measures to reduce energy demand and emissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If you have not been to SDC recently, I encourage you to do so and, perhaps, I can invite and organise Members in this House, if you are interested, for a visit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Museums and galleries are wonderful channels to learn about defence, as history offers important lessons while we look ahead to chart our course in an uncertain, ever-surprising future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We hope that visitors will walk away with an understanding of the competing needs, goals and trade-offs that we have made as a nation and those we might make in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, every Singaporean must understand Singapore’s security environment, unique vulnerabilities and the roles that we can play.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Only then can we recognise the opportunities to contribute and step up where needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am grateful to our ACCORD partners, who are instrumental in this effort, and have been reaching out to more youths and women in their current term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They have conducted NS engagement talks, a webinar series on NS and defence issues for University undergraduates and grassroots dialogues with women.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through these efforts, we prepare those who need to serve NS and help their families and friends take steps to support them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There is a part for everyone to play, no matter how small, to make our defence total.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Member Carrie Tan had shown interest and asked if MINDEF would consider expanding NS to include community care roles and enlist both men and women.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NS is based on the critical need of national security and defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Currently, our NS population adequately meets our national security and defence needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Both Minister Ng Eng Hen and Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How have spoken about MINDEF and the SAF's continued efforts to enhance manpower resource efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, contributing to Singapore's defence should not be limited to just those serving NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There are many different opportunities for Singaporeans to contribute actively through Total Defence and I encourage everyone to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One example is by equipping oneself with practical emergency response skills for Civil Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This year, we commemorate 55 years of National Service (NS), as both Minister Ng Eng Heng and Senior Minister Heng Chee How have mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NS has been the bedrock of our defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Generation after generation have served, first as NSFs, then as NSmen, to protect and defend Singapore's interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: That is why it is important to appreciate the dedication, service and sacrifice of our National Servicemen and to thank them for their efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Members Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim and Yeo Wan Ling asked about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also expand the spaces for Singaporeans to reflect on the significance of NS, whether through close engagement with our youths or experiential camps for families and the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More details on the initiatives will be shared later in the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The three SAF Services will also continue to engage the community, such as through their open houses and charity events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We recognise that the security challenges we face are immense and constantly evolving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MINDEF will continue to build Total Defence as our best response to the threats and challenges that might come our way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am heartened that Singaporeans want to do their part for Total Defence through understanding and action and we will partner you to work towards securing our collective future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: By working together, we have every reason to be confident that we will keep Singapore strong today and for generations to come.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I am looking forward to using the new equipment, if it is available.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The second, of course, is just to seek clarification that training has been going on smoothly with COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As you go out on the various rings, ensure that there are both processes as well as outcomes that measure that your units are up to date.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is not always possible for a large military – for us, we are a small military but a large organisation – that you can equip all the units at the same time.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, it is not as if all units are using the same level of advanced equipment.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, in a nutshell, it is always a challenge but I think the SAF, by and large, across all units, do quite well.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It helps that we also have a young military, in a sense that, on average, In-Camp Trainings (ICTs) are across 10 years.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Vikram Nair, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: With that, Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
